environment.description: Application deployed identically but fronted by CloudFront distribution with AWS WAF WebACL. The WebACL has three rule groups evaluated in priority order: (1) AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet at priority 100 in COUNT mode for baseline telemetry, (2) a custom rule group 'corp-input-validation' at priority 200 containing a single RegexPatternSet rule matching request query string parameters against pattern `(?i)(?:union\s+select|;\s*(?:drop|alter|insert|update|delete)|'\s*or\s+'|sleep\s*\(|benchmark\s*\()` with action BLOCK and label 'corp:sqli:query-param', (3) AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet at priority 300 with all rules in BLOCK mode including SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS, SQLi_BODY, and SQLi_COOKIE inspection. CloudFront origin is configured with custom header x-origin-verify that nginx validates before proxying, preventing direct origin access bypass.

config.cdn: CloudFront distribution with origin access via custom header verification
config.waf_webacl: AWS WAF v2 WebACL attached to CloudFront
config.waf_rule_2: Custom rule group 'corp-input-validation' priority=200, RegexPatternSet on QueryString, action=BLOCK
config.waf_rule_3: AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet priority=300 action=BLOCK (all rules enabled including SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS)
config.origin_protection: CloudFront sends x-origin-verify header; nginx returns 403 if header missing/invalid
config.compute: EC2 t3.medium, Amazon Linux 2023, SG allows 443 only from CloudFront managed prefix list
config.database: SQLite 3.40 on local EBS gp3 volume
